evidence: http.py:274-281: ASGI http.response.start 'headers' is an iterable of [name, value] byte-string pairs, with lowercase names. The code copies the message, filters existing pairs with k.lower() != b'x-sqllens-auth' (k is bytes, so this is valid), and appends a (bytes, bytes) tuple. The result is a list of bytes pairs, which is valid for downstream send. message.get('headers', []) handles a missing key. The rejection line concerns construction-time warnings, not this claim.

http.py:235-239: TrustedHostMiddleware(_InsecureAuthMarker(_PathNormalizer(_AuthMiddleware(inner)))). Marker (255-283) wraps send for every http scope and stamps X-SQLLens-Auth on http.response.start (replacing duplicates), so any response generated by _PathNormalizer (/healthz, /readyz, / 307) or _AuthMiddleware (401) passes through marked_send. TrustedHostMiddleware is outermost and on a bad Host sends its own 400 without calling the inner app, so the marker never runs for those. Marker is applied only when insecure_bind (line 238), which is the scenario the claim describes. The rejection about construction-time warnings is unrelated to this ordering claim.
